title: Ending an old rule and keeping closeness

captions.physics: Rejecting entertainment that no longer works
captions.energy: Expecting shared wishes to remain identical

meaning: Shared joy gains room for change when ending an unworkable entertainment remains free from proving that mutual desire has disappeared.
text: An earlier entertainment can survive through a mistaken idea of you both. The Tower in the physical position of Svadhisthana describes rejecting a programme that ceased to work. The Lovers in energy lean towards expecting wishes to match unchanged, as though familiar pleasure must always appeal equally. Death in emotions allows the ending of one particular joy to be experienced. The roles differ: stopping a failed action, meeting a demand for unity and feeling a familiar ending. None determines your future closeness or pleasure.

Suppose a usual quiz evening has become tense scoring and attempts not to disappoint the other. **Ending one entertainment need not reject enjoyment together.** You can put cards away and acknowledge wanting something different. Earlier good evenings remain valuable within shared experience even before another permanent leisure form is known. Hearing today’s wishes is sufficient, beyond immediately proving that a replacement will please both forever.

The difficulty is forcing familiar enjoyment to return through repetition. You bring cards out again to test an earlier feeling and experience different interest more painfully. Ending acquires extra meaning. Rejecting the false condition helps when the past can remain valuable and finished. Both may miss it and freely choose less. Closeness need not resemble the former game; a quiet meeting can matter without restoring identical excitement.
